10 [RETRACTION 2026-07-16c — owner: 'แบบมันไม่ได้ผิด แต่เครื่องมืออ่านแบบของเราห่วย'. He was right; every claim below is WITHDRAWN.] THE TEST: measured each BF piece's drawn extent against its OWN printed label — BF14 3250.2 vs 3250 (+0.2), BF13 4100.8 vs 4100 (+0.8), BF09-3 3301.0 vs 3300 (+1.0), BF12-2 701.5 vs 700 (+1.5), BF09-2 1498.1 vs 1500 (-1.9), BF10 2497.9 vs 2500 (-2.1), BF12-1 1577.5 vs 1575 (+2.5), ensuite counter 3047.0 vs printed '3.05' (-3.0). **The sheet agrees with itself to <=2.5 mm (0.16%). Our spec disagreed with the sheet by up to 2850 mm.** ~1000x. Every discrepancy this session resolved to OUR reader, never the drawing. WITHDRAWN: (i) 'BF09-1's east leg is drawn through the y5697.9 column with no notch = a real build clash' — a 1:75 FURNITURE plan does not draw notches (101.6 = 1.3 mm on paper); that belongs to the joinery drawing. Wrong document tier, not an error. (ii) 'the sheet REFUSES to draw a pocket' — a furniture plan never carries a pocket cage. (iii) 'BF09-3's 3 equal bays CONTRADICT the signed asymmetric layout' — those are drawn carcass/module lines, not a design instruction. (iv) 'BF09-1 is 26.4 short of its 5200 label' — 26.4 = 1.7 pen widths, and it depends on a corner-counting convention the reader does not know. (v) 'nothing explains the wall step' — structural wall vs partition; only a tool with no concept of buildings calls that unexplained. ROOT CAUSE: the reader has no notion of DRAWING TIER or PEN RESOLUTION. At 1:75 a 0.6pt stroke covers 15.87 mm of real space, yet I reported the leaf lane gap (9.5 = 0.60 pen) and y-lap (12.7 = 0.80 pen) as findings — precision that does not exist. Worse, I told the adversarial refuters to 'default to refuted unless reproducible from a dump', which auto-kills every non-stroke claim; the 50/94 refutation rate was that bias, not rigour. THE RULE (see also memory 'drawing-tier-law'): this sheet answers WHERE / HOW BIG / WHAT IT IS CALLED, to ~2.5 mm — which is more than enough. Notches, pocket cages, head heights and joinery are NOT in it, and their absence is not a gap, a conflict, or anyone's error: they are ours to DESIGN or the owner's/designer's to answer. Never again generate a 'designer error' list from a document that was never asked the question.

The y110 trim was MY error: y110 carries ZERO horizontal strokes anywhere on this floor (`ink.py -500 11000 105 120 0` → 0 horizontals), y-275 likewise matches nothing, and both BF14 faces run through y110 as UNBROKEN 3250.2 lines with a drawn south cap at y-450.2. The owner's '~y110' was RIGHT but about a DIFFERENT OBJECT — see curtain_track.owner_y110_referent. w kept at 100, NOT 98.4: the sheet snaps to a ~3.174 mm (0.12pt) grid on which 100 (31.506 quanta) is unrepresentable, so a drawn 100 reads 98.4 or 101.6 and adjacent pairs sum to exactly 200.0 — 98.4 IS a drawn 100. design.decision: D2-A SUPERSEDED 2026-07-16c — owner chose the AKUWALL product BY LOOKING at an A/B render pair ('ผมชอบ akuwall'), which is the only design instrument he can actually operate (he is an engineer, not a designer — see corrections_applied #11). product.build: 9 mm polyester-fibre acoustic base + 12 mm MDF slat = 21 mm total

product.backing: black (delivers D2-A's matte-black backer as a product, not a bespoke detail)

product.price_caveat: catalogue 2023, VAT status unstated — the vault header flags its pricing as stale. NOT a quote.
product.why_this_won: owner answered YES to an acoustic requirement (2026-07-16c). The bespoke 40/20's signed matte-black PLY backer is a REFLECTOR — slats + gaps absorb nothing against solid ply — so 'yes' forced either a porous backer with zero vault data, or this product. It also carries the only fire data we have, a real price, a real SKU and a 15-day lead, which serves the sourceability north-star.

schedule.posts_note: 79.6 = 1.99 x the 40 mm pitch, so each terminus reads as two beats of the field's own rhythm rather than as leftover. The remainder is sunk into TIMBER, not into air — no part-slat, no tuned face, no tuned gap.
schedule.reveal_note: 12.0 is the OWNER'S engineering call 2026-07-16c ('12 / เสา 63'): 15 sat at the very top of the 10-15 window with zero site tolerance, so a wavy plastered ceiling pushes it out of window; 12 is mid-window with +/-3. He answered the post number for the 40/20 field (63); the module change recomputes it to 79.6 — his decision was the REVEAL, the post is its consequence.
schedule.d7_decision: D7 DECIDED 2026-07-16c by CLAUDE, not by menu. The owner is an engineer, not a designer (corrections_applied #11), and this DD's own D7 note says: stop issuing A/B/C menus of taste for signature; decide it, build it, render it, put the PICTURE in front of him. B = MINERAL RELEASE: the south jamb is cool microcement, the north terminus is oak. The north end is oak into oak, a JOINT, because BF09-3 receives it; the south end has nothing to receive it (248 of air, then black alu, then garden) so it is RELEASED, not received. WHAT THE OWNER'S AUTHORITY DOES *NOT* COVER HERE: his 'ไม่น่าใช่เสาไม้' answered NORTH POST solid-oak-vs-veneer and was resolved to VENEER (which postoak builds). It rules out SOLID oak, nothing more; citing it against wood ENTIRELY at the south would borrow his authority for a call he never made. The wood-vs-mineral choice is a CLAUDE DESIGN call, owned as one. WHY B: (1) the received/released asymmetry IS the design; (2) D1-A anti-monopoly — an oak jamb stands 0.27 m2 of warm oak in the room's only cool aperture, bouncing warm GI into the 60% plaster ground exactly where D1-A must prove itself; (3) it is the smooth hard cheek the curtain slides past (77 open 13 mm gaps at a curtain mouth is a fabric snag — weaker than at 40/20, stated not leaned on). REJECTED: A solid oak post (vault rates ไม้จริง Poor for dimensional movement, residential-materials.md:43-44, at the room's sunniest/wettest/most thermally cycled point — and NOT 'the mirror of the north', which is veneer); A-prime an oak-VENEER jamb = the REAL mirror and the honest competitor, which loses to B on the design legs (1)+(2) alone and is the fallback if B fails on site; C black-anodised alu (folded 5005/5052 sheet vs extruded 6063 frames — black anodic film does not match across alloy families, so a THIRD black 292 mm from the frames it was built to join = D1-C smuggled in through a detail).
schedule.d7_geometry_note: SUPERSEDES D7-B item 1's dimensions, which are the DEAD 40/20 schedule's: 60.0 -> 79.6 (the AKUWALL module's terminal member) and 2770 -> 2776 (reveal 12, not 15). Depth = the bbox's full 100, NOT the ink's 98.4 — the spec already decided 98.4 IS a drawn 100 (see this builtin's note). STILL LIVE from D7-B and NOT built: the mineral lining continuing north as the curtain slot's west cheek (y-450.2->149.7, 599.9 — behind BF14, no camera sees it); R6-R10 arris on the mineral vs 1.5-2.0 chamfer on the slats (build_room gives every mill part the same 1.2 mm arris); 'nothing wet happens inside the slot' is a drawing note, not geometry. D7-B item 7's curtain lock is WITHDRAWN by owner answer (5) and is deliberately NOT encoded.

design.material_intent: AKUWALL imported natural-oak veneer face over its own engineered build — satisfies the D5-A intent (veneer over engineered core, NOT solid oak) as a bought product rather than a bespoke mill run
design.build_layer_gap: CLOSED 2026-07-16c. millwork.py used to auto-fit (n = int(run // (face+gap)); pitch = run/n over the WHOLE run) -> 81 slats @ pitch 40.123 with 6.56 mm end margins, NOT the issued 77 + two terminal members + 12 reveals. (This note and the DD both said 10.06 — WRONG: 10.06 is (40.12-20)/2, the DEAD 40/20 gap arithmetic carried over by hand; at face 27 the real margin is (40.123-27)/2 = 6.56.) The A/B render the owner chose the module from (room_bedroom_suite_eye_akuwall.png) WAS that 81-slat auto-fit — nobody was misled, the MODULE is what he judged and it is right, but no render had ever shown the issued wall. millwork.slat_schedule_setout now reads this schedule block and emits it: 77 slats at a TRUE 40 pitch (field butted, 77x27+76x13 = 3067.0 exact), a 79.6 microcement south jamb, a north terminus SCRIBED to whatever run remains (79.4 against this spec's nominal d=3250 — a literal 79.6 ends at 3250.2, overruns the bbox and part() SILENTLY DROPS it, i.e. a render quietly missing a member that still looks fine; the 0.2 dies in the north scribe, exactly where the DD says it must), and the 12 reveals at floor + ceiling giving the 2776 cut length. Every number this block STATES (field_mm, cut_length_mm, post_north_mm) and BOTH terminal materials are REQUIRED and re-derived — a spec edited without re-issuing the schedule RAISES instead of rendering a different wall.
